title: How Ankur describes his work
text:
The portfolio presents Ankur as someone working across software systems, books, and independent conceptual research. He builds Ezra, a readable scripting language and compiler/virtual machine in Rust, alongside real-world full-stack platforms. His writing ranges from questions about time and reality to attention, relationships, Hindi poetry, and Awadhi language and heritage.
His stated development stance is that AI is a collaborative development partner and intellectual accelerator, while he owns the requirements, product direction, architectural choices, understanding, testing, and final result. He describes AI as a collaborator while retaining ownership of judgment and responsibility.

title: Research and intellectual interests
text:
Time: physical structure, subjective experience, historical measurement, and conceptual mystery.
Reality: models, assumptions, perception, and layers of interpretation.
Consciousness and human perception: awareness, memory, attention, and the filters that shape what people notice and recall.
Psychology: focus, overthinking, emotional patterns, relationship behavior, and modern life.
Philosophy: meaning, identity, love, discipline, culture, and human questions.
Language: cultural memory and living identity, especially the preservation and teaching of Awadhi.
Portfolio quote: “Understanding begins when we stop treating the mind, time, love, and language as separate mysteries.”

title: How he works with AI
text: The published workflow has nine steps: define an idea and success; specify testable requirements; research approaches and constraints; make architecture decisions; use AI-assisted implementation; test; debug root causes; iterate from real use and feedback; deploy and maintain. The portfolio specifically assigns architecture and responsibility to Ankur.

title: Ezra
text:
A readable scripting language and developer ecosystem built in Rust. The project is explicitly positioned as a way to understand the whole language pipeline and to make a useful, readability-first toolchain.
Current portfolio status: Live (as listed in the portfolio; deployment can change).
Design principle: Readable source and a smooth developer experience take priority over sacrificing clarity for performance.
Pipeline: Source → lexer → parser → abstract syntax tree → compiler → bytecode → stack-based virtual machine → output.
Features: Lexer, parser, AST, compiler, bytecode VM, CLI, standard library, formatter, linter/static analysis, VS Code extension with syntax highlighting and LSP/error support, documentation site, and interactive browser IDE (profile README).
Reported engineering challenges: Designing an expressive but unambiguous grammar; implementing a correct bytecode compiler; getting VM control flow, functions, and closures right; delivering VS Code tooling and LSP support.
Reported learning: End-to-end language implementation, Rust ownership/type system, compiler decisions across the toolchain, and the discipline of shipping developer tools for other people.
Stack: Rust, TypeScript, Next.js, Vercel; compiler and VM implementation in Rust.
Live documentation / site: https://ezra-programming-lang.vercel.app/
GitHub repository: https://github.com/ranaji114/Ezra-programming-lang
The GitHub profile README uses some performance and implementation claims (for example opcode counts and execution time) that are not independently validated in this dossier. Those performance figures are presented in the README and have not been independently validated in this dossier.

title: Maa Sarswati Digital Library — Live in portfolio
text:
A digital study-library platform for a library in MudilaDeeh, Kadipur, Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh. The product covers public information and owner workflows for membership, student admissions, notices, reviews, and gallery content.
Public features: Facilities, membership plans, photo gallery, live notices, contact enquiries, and student rating/review flow.
Admissions: Online registration with photo and Aadhaar document upload handled as multipart data via Multer and validation.
Administration: JWT-protected dashboard to approve/reject admissions, manage students, notices, reviews, gallery, and enquiries; repository/portfolio mentions rate limits, bcrypt, Zod, Helmet, and Cloudinary.
Architecture: React/Vite single-page frontend on Vercel → Express 5 ESM REST API on Render → Supabase PostgreSQL. The listed architecture includes JWT and bcrypt, Multer upload handling, and an admin login.
Challenges / learning: Multipart uploads on mobile connections; CORS and trust-proxy/rate-limit configuration across hosts; mobile viewport behavior; deployment across frontend, API, and database.
Stack: React 19, Vite 7, Express 5, Node.js, Supabase PostgreSQL, Tailwind CSS, Multer, JWT, Render, Vercel
GitHub: https://github.com/ranaji114/Ma-Sarswati-Digital-Library
Live: https://ma-sarswati-digital-library-fronten.vercel.app

title: The Unknowable Reality
text:
Subtitle: The Evolution of Intelligence, Knowledge, and the Limits of Understanding
Category / reading style: Science and Philosophy · Deep read
Core premise: Why intelligence—human or artificial—may never fully grasp the reality it inhabits.
Examines the co-evolution of intelligence and knowledge across biology, science, philosophy, and AI. Its central proposition is that limits of understanding may be structural features of a mind modelling a reality larger than itself, rather than temporary gaps that more information alone will remove.
Themes: Intelligence; knowledge; epistemology; philosophy of mind.
Why a reader might choose it: Readers interested in boundaries of intelligence; connections between cognitive science, philosophy of science, and AI; and challenges to the idea that more information guarantees deeper understanding.
Related titles in the portfolio: The Architecture of Existence; The World Through Our Mind; The Attention Asset
Metadata: Listed as latest title; publication date 30 July 2026; 169 pages; English.
Amazon: https://amzn.in/d/06YNVlNC

title: The Architecture of Existence
text:
Subtitle: The Biography of Time
Category / reading style: Science and Philosophy · Deep read
Core premise: A sweeping journey through the question: what is time?
Moves from ancient shadow clocks and sacred calendars to Einstein, black holes, quantum mechanics, multiverses, and loop quantum gravity. It frames time as scientific mystery and philosophical biography, connecting memory, causality, entropy, relativity, and the possibility that time is real but not fundamental.
Themes: Time; physics; cosmology; metaphysics.
Why a reader might choose it: A flagship, ambitious work for readers who want the history and science of time without heavy mathematics, joining civilizations, paradoxes, and modern physics in one readable arc.
Related titles in the portfolio: The World Through Our Mind; The Attention Asset; Learn Awadhi

title: Ankur Rana's portfolio website
text:
PURPOSE: This is Ankur Rana's personal portfolio: a public home for his software projects, books, independent research, professional background, philosophy, and ways to contact him. It is designed for readers, potential collaborators, recruiters, and visitors curious about his work. Public URL: https://ankur-rana.vercel.app/ . The portfolio is a presentation of Ankur's work, not a separate product or company.
PAGES: Home (/), About (/about), Work (/work), Books (/books), Research (/research), and Contact (/contact), with individual case studies under /work/<project-slug>. The home page introduces Ankur, showcases projects, explains his AI-assisted development workflow, highlights a book and research papers, and ends with his philosophy and collaboration invitation.
WORK: Five detailed project case studies: Ezra, Shri Krishna Coaching Center, Maa Sarswati Digital Library, Vani, and Al-Farooq. Source content marks the first three as live and Vani and Al-Farooq as archived; deployment status can change. Case studies describe each project's purpose, design decisions, architecture, technologies, features, challenges, learning, and links. Ezra also has an interactive in-browser language playground.
BOOKS AND RESEARCH: The Books page catalogs seven published titles across science, philosophy, attention, relationships, Hindi poetry, and Awadhi language, with book previews and Amazon links. The Research page presents two conceptual papers about quantum entanglement and temporal perception, with Zenodo links and an interactive topic map. These papers are Ankur's independent proposals, not established scientific consensus.
INTERACTIONS: The site includes a cinematic home introduction with three identity views (Unified Identity, Systems Dev, Author), responsive navigation, dark/light themes, a command palette, scroll progress, subtle sound controls, animated scroll reveals, an interactive nine-step Human-AI development workflow, project demonstrations, and book previews. Motion respects reduced-motion preferences and the layout adapts to phones.
CONTACT: The Contact page has an inquiry form for projects, jobs/internships, collaboration, research, writing/books, and other messages, plus direct contact and social links.
IMPLEMENTATION: Built with Next.js App Router 16.2, React 19, TypeScript, custom CSS, and Motion for React. The public pages are prerendered where possible; the voice assistant uses server-side API routes. The project is configured for Vercel deployment. The floating assistant is voice-first: visitors grant microphone permission, speak questions about Ankur and his public work, see speech/reply captions, and hear a spoken response. Deployment and provider configuration can change.
